full_text: WOR REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahai St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG Legal Opinion No. 17 s. 2012 FEB 24 Mr. Abraenian Tingguian abraeni antingguian@yahoo.com Dear Mr. Tingguian, This pertains to your e-mail query on whether a Sangguniang Bayan Secretary may be designated as OIC Municipal Treasurer, which is allegedly the present situation in the Municipality of Licuan-Baay, Province of Abra. In reply thereto, please be informed that this Department already had the occasion to clarify the issue regarding the prohibition on appointment of elective or appointive local officials in DILG Legal Opinion No. 61, s. 2008, a copy of which is posted at this Department's website www.dilg.gov.ph, and available for download thereat. The said opinion merely stated the rule under Section 94 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, which states that no elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Aside from the said provision, the third paragraph Of Section 7, Article IX-B of the 1987 Philippine Constitution provides: "Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no appointive official shaZZ hold any other office or employment in the government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controtZed corporations or their subsidiaries. In view of the foregoing, it is clear that the Sangguniang Bayan Secretary, during his tenure as such, cannot be appointed or designated in any capacity to any other public office or position such as OIC Municipal Treasurer. Finally, since it can be inferred from your letter that it was the Municipal Mayor who designated the Sangguniang Bayan Secretary as OIC Municipal Treasurer, please be advised that paragraph (a), Section 470 of RA 7160 states that the treasurer shall be appointed by the Secretary of Finance from a list of at least three (3) ranking, eligible recommendees of the governor or mayor, as the case may be, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, ESUS D Dir ctor 11 Legal:03
